newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent products differentials steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent products differentials steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel basis tracked futures prices late Friday on unchanged differentials inggish trade, traders said.
Looking ahead to next week, traders said ample gasoline stocks and diminishing agricultural demand for diesel barrels were expected to weaken basis on October refined products.
"Agricultural demand is winding down," a Kansas City, Mo., trader said. Trade this week was thinned by two outings that pulled dozens of traders out of the Chicago and Group Three markets.
Turnarounds were not seen as a factor in the market next week. Turnarounds were completed this week at Farmland's Coffeyville, Kansas and Mobil's Joliet, Ill., refineries, traders said.
The Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of inventories in the Midwest, reported a 21-day supply of gasoline and 28-day supply of low sulphur diesel on hand.

"Chicago has a glut of high sulphur diesel," another trader said. High sulphur diesel for October deliveries was talked 5.0/4.50 cents under the print in Chicago and 1.5/1.0 cent under in Group Three.
Prompt unleaded gasoline was steady at 1.50/1.25 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 1.0/0.75 cent under the print in Group Three.
Prompt low sulphur diesel remained bid 2.50 cents under the print in Chicago and even to the print in Group Three, traders said.
Jet/kero for all October timings was talked 0.50 cent over the print in Chicago and 0.75 cent over in Group Three.
